Measurements and Units.text: The instrument most suitable for measuring the diameter of a thin wire is the
options: metre rule
vernier calipers
micrometer screw gauge
measuring cylinder
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: micrometer screw gauge

Measurements and Units.text: Vernier calipers are most suitable for measuring
options: the diameter of a very thin wire
small lengths and internal/external diameters with moderate precision
volumes of gases
time intervals
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: small lengths and internal/external diameters with moderate precision

Measurements and Units.text: The SI unit of mass is the
options: newton
kilogram
gram
pound
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: kilogram

Measurements and Units.text: A simple beam balance is used to measure
options: weight directly
mass, by comparison with known standard masses
volume
density directly without calculation
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: mass, by comparison with known standard masses

Measurements and Units.text: The SI unit of time is the
options: minute
hour
second
day
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: second

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following is a fundamental physical quantity?
options: Velocity
Force
Length
Momentum
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Length

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following is a derived physical quantity?
options: Mass
Length
Time
Velocity
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Velocity

Measurements and Units.text: The dimension of velocity is
options: [LT⁻¹]
[LT⁻²]
[MLT⁻¹]
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: [LT⁻¹]

Measurements and Units.text: The dimension of acceleration is
options: [LT⁻¹]
[LT⁻²]
[MLT⁻²]
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: [LT⁻²]

Measurements and Units.text: The dimension of force is
options: [LT⁻²]
[MLT⁻²]
[MLT⁻¹]
[ML²T⁻²]
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: [MLT⁻²]

Measurements and Units.text: Dimensional analysis is useful mainly for
options: determining the exact numerical value of a physical constant
checking the homogeneity (consistency) of a physical equation
measuring time intervals directly
calibrating a thermometer
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: checking the homogeneity (consistency) of a physical equation

Measurements and Units.text: The number of significant figures in the measurement 0.00420 is
Expressing 45000 in standard form gives
The accuracy of a measuring instrument refers to
options: how many times it can be reused
how close a measured value is to the true value
its cost
its physical size
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: how close a measured value is to the true value

Measurements and Units.text: A systematic error in measurement is one that
options: varies randomly from one reading to another
consistently occurs in the same direction, often due to a fault in the instrument or method
cannot occur in careful experiments
only occurs with digital instruments
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: consistently occurs in the same direction, often due to a fault in the instrument or method

Measurements and Units.text: Displacement is best described as
options: the total path length covered by a body, regardless of direction
the shortest distance between initial and final position, in a specified direction
always equal to distance travelled
a scalar quantity
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: the shortest distance between initial and final position, in a specified direction

Measurements and Units.text: Distance differs from displacement in that distance is a
options: vector quantity, while displacement is scalar
scalar quantity, while displacement is a vector quantity with direction
always identical quantity to displacement
quantity that cannot be measured
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: scalar quantity, while displacement is a vector quantity with direction

Measurements and Units.text: A frame of reference is best described as
options: a coordinate system relative to which the position and motion of a body are described
a type of measuring instrument
a unit of time
a fixed value that never changes
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: a coordinate system relative to which the position and motion of a body are described

Measurements and Units.text: The position of a point in a plane can be located using
options: only a single number
Cartesian coordinates (x, y) relative to chosen axes
mass alone
time alone
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Cartesian coordinates (x, y) relative to chosen axes

Measurements and Units.text: A measuring cylinder is primarily used to determine the
options: mass of a solid
volume of a liquid, or the volume of an irregular solid by displacement
time taken for an event
temperature of a substance
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: volume of a liquid, or the volume of an irregular solid by displacement

Measurements and Units.text: To find the volume of an irregularly shaped solid, a suitable method is
options: using a metre rule directly
the displacement method using a measuring cylinder or eureka can
using a stopwatch
using a thermometer
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: the displacement method using a measuring cylinder or eureka can

Measurements and Units.text: The zero error of a measuring instrument refers to
options: the reading obtained when the instrument should read exactly zero but does not
the maximum possible reading of the instrument
an error that can never be corrected
the reading obtained only at very high temperatures
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: the reading obtained when the instrument should read exactly zero but does not

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following combinations correctly deduces the unit of a derived quantity, using density as an example?
options: Density = mass/volume, so its unit is kg/m³, derived from the fundamental units of mass and length
Density has no relationship to fundamental units
Density’s unit is always the newton
Density is itself a fundamental quantity
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Density = mass/volume, so its unit is kg/m³, derived from the fundamental units of mass and length

Measurements and Units.text: The dimension of energy (work done) is
options: [MLT⁻¹]
[ML²T⁻²]
[MLT⁻²]
[ML²T⁻¹]
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: [ML²T⁻²]

Measurements and Units.text: Testing the homogeneity of a physical equation using dimensions means checking that
options: both sides of the equation have the same numerical value
both sides of the equation have the same dimensions
the equation contains only fundamental quantities
the equation has no derived quantities at all
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: both sides of the equation have the same dimensions

Measurements and Units.text: A stopwatch is a device used to measure
options: mass
short time intervals with reasonable precision
length
temperature
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: short time intervals with reasonable precision

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following is an example of a derived unit?
options: Kilogram
Metre
Newton (kg m s⁻²)
Second
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Newton (kg m s⁻²)

Measurements and Units.text: The main advantage of expressing very large or very small numbers in standard form is that it
options: makes numbers appear larger than they actually are
simplifies representation and calculation, and clearly shows the number of significant figures
eliminates the need for units
is only used for whole numbers
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: simplifies representation and calculation, and clearly shows the number of significant figures

Measurements and Units.text: Random errors in measurement can generally be reduced by
options: using a single measurement only
taking multiple readings and calculating the average
ignoring the measurement process entirely
always using the same faulty instrument
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: taking multiple readings and calculating the average

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following correctly lists the seven SI fundamental (base) quantities as recognized in physics: length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance, and
options: velocity
luminous intensity
force
energy
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: luminous intensity

Measurements and Units.text: A Cartesian coordinate system is useful in physics mainly for
options: measuring mass directly
precisely specifying the position of a point in a plane or space relative to reference axes
measuring temperature
measuring current
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: precisely specifying the position of a point in a plane or space relative to reference axes

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following correctly explains why estimating experimental errors is an important part of practical physics?
options: It has no bearing on the reliability of experimental results
It allows an assessment of how much confidence can be placed in a measured or calculated result
Errors are always negligible and therefore not worth estimating
Only theoretical physics requires error estimation
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: It allows an assessment of how much confidence can be placed in a measured or calculated result

Scalars and Vectors.text: A scalar quantity is one that has
options: magnitude and direction
magnitude only, with no direction
direction only, with no magnitude
neither magnitude nor direction
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: magnitude only, with no direction

Scalars and Vectors.text: A vector quantity is one that has
options: magnitude only
both magnitude and direction
neither magnitude nor direction
direction only, with no magnitude
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: both magnitude and direction

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
options: Velocity
Displacement
Mass
Force
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: Mass

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
options: Mass
Time
Force
Energy
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: Force

Scalars and Vectors.text: Speed and velocity differ in that
options: speed is a vector and velocity is a scalar
speed is a scalar (magnitude only), while velocity is a vector (magnitude and direction)
they are identical in every respect
neither has a defined magnitude
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: speed is a scalar (magnitude only), while velocity is a vector (magnitude and direction)

Scalars and Vectors.text: The resultant of two vectors acting in the same direction is found by
options: subtracting their magnitudes
adding their magnitudes directly
multiplying their magnitudes
taking the difference of their squares
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: adding their magnitudes directly

Scalars and Vectors.text: The resultant of two vectors acting in exactly opposite directions is found by
options: adding their magnitudes
subtracting the smaller magnitude from the larger, in the direction of the larger
multiplying their magnitudes
always equal to zero
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: subtracting the smaller magnitude from the larger, in the direction of the larger

Scalars and Vectors.text: Two vectors acting at an angle to each other can be combined using
options: simple addition of magnitudes only
the parallelogram law of vector addition
subtraction only
they cannot be combined at all
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: the parallelogram law of vector addition

Scalars and Vectors.text: Relative velocity refers to the
options: velocity of a body measured from a fixed, absolute frame only
velocity of one body as observed from another moving body (reference frame)
velocity of a stationary body
sum of all velocities in a system regardless of frame
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: velocity of one body as observed from another moving body (reference frame)

Scalars and Vectors.text: Resolving a vector into two perpendicular components means
options: combining two vectors into one
splitting a single vector into two component vectors along chosen perpendicular axes
reversing the direction of the vector
doubling the magnitude of the vector
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: splitting a single vector into two component vectors along chosen perpendicular axes

Scalars and Vectors.text: If a vector of magnitude F acts at angle θ to the horizontal, its horizontal component is
options: F sin θ
F cos θ
F tan θ
F
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: F cos θ

Scalars and Vectors.text: If a vector of magnitude F acts at angle θ to the horizontal, its vertical component is
options: F cos θ
F sin θ
F tan θ
F
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: F sin θ

Scalars and Vectors.text: A graphical method of vector addition involves
options: drawing vectors to scale, tail to head, and measuring the resultant directly from the diagram
only using algebraic formulas, with no diagrams
ignoring direction entirely
using only scalar quantities
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: drawing vectors to scale, tail to head, and measuring the resultant directly from the diagram

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following is an example of relative velocity in everyday experience?
options: The speed of a car as measured by a stationary observer only
The apparent velocity of a passing car as observed from inside a moving vehicle
Mass measured on a scale
Temperature measured with a thermometer
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: The apparent velocity of a passing car as observed from inside a moving vehicle

Scalars and Vectors.text: Two perpendicular vectors of magnitude 3 units and 4 units have a resultant magnitude of
options: 5 units
7 units
1 unit
12 units
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: 5 units

Scalars and Vectors.text: The direction of the resultant vector, when combining two perpendicular vectors, can be found using
options: simple addition alone
trigonometric ratios, such as tan⁻¹(opposite/adjacent)
multiplication of magnitudes
it cannot be determined
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: trigonometric ratios, such as tan⁻¹(opposite/adjacent)

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following best describes the “triangle law” of vector addition?
options: If two vectors are represented as two sides of a triangle taken in order, the resultant is represented by the third side, taken in the opposite order
The triangle law only applies to scalar quantities
Vectors cannot be added using triangles
The triangle law gives only the magnitude, never the direction
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: If two vectors are represented as two sides of a triangle taken in order, the resultant is represented by the third side, taken in the opposite order

Scalars and Vectors.text: Weight is classified as a vector quantity because it has
options: magnitude only
both magnitude and a specific direction (downward, toward the Earth’s centre)
no defined magnitude
no relationship to force
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: both magnitude and a specific direction (downward, toward the Earth’s centre)

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following is NOT typically classified as a vector quantity in elementary mechanics?
options: Displacement
Acceleration
Energy
Momentum
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: Energy

Scalars and Vectors.text: The equilibrant of a system of forces is a single force that
options: has the same magnitude and direction as the resultant
has the same magnitude as the resultant but acts in the exact opposite direction, bringing the system into equilibrium
has no relationship to the resultant force
is always zero
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: has the same magnitude as the resultant but acts in the exact opposite direction, bringing the system into equilibrium

Scalars and Vectors.text: Resolving forces into perpendicular components is particularly useful for
options: simplifying the analysis of forces acting at angles, by treating horizontal and vertical effects separately
eliminating the need to consider direction at all
converting vector quantities into purely scalar quantities with no further use
situations involving only a single force acting along one axis
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: simplifying the analysis of forces acting at angles, by treating horizontal and vertical effects separately

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following correctly identifies a physical situation requiring the concept of relative velocity?
options: Determining how fast a boat appears to move relative to the riverbank, accounting for the river’s current
Measuring the mass of an object at rest
Measuring the temperature of a room
Measuring the volume of an irregular solid
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: Determining how fast a boat appears to move relative to the riverbank, accounting for the river’s current

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following correctly explains why vector addition cannot generally be performed by simple arithmetic addition of magnitudes alone, unless the vectors are collinear?
options: Direction must be taken into account, since vectors combine according to their directions as well as magnitudes
Vectors have no direction, so simple addition always works
Vector addition is identical to scalar addition in all cases
Only the smaller vector’s magnitude matters in vector addition
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: Direction must be taken into account, since vectors combine according to their directions as well as magnitudes

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the practical importance of resolving vectors and combining them via graphical or analytical methods in physics problems, such as projectile motion or equilibrium of forces?
options: It allows complex multi-directional force or motion problems to be broken down into manageable, independent perpendicular components for easier analysis
Vector resolution has no practical application in solving physics problems
All physics problems can be solved without any consideration of vector direction
Vector methods apply only to purely theoretical, non-applied physics
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: It allows complex multi-directional force or motion problems to be broken down into manageable, independent perpendicular components for easier analysis

Motion.text: Translational motion refers to motion in which
options: a body rotates about a fixed axis
every part of a body moves the same distance in the same direction
a body moves back and forth repeatedly
motion occurs with no defined pattern
Motion.correct_answer: every part of a body moves the same distance in the same direction

Motion.text: Oscillatory motion refers to motion that is
options: always in a straight line without repetition
repetitive, back-and-forth about a fixed point or equilibrium position
always circular
completely random and unpredictable
Motion.correct_answer: repetitive, back-and-forth about a fixed point or equilibrium position

Motion.text: Rotational motion refers to motion in which a body
options: moves along a straight line only
turns about a fixed axis
moves randomly with no defined path
remains completely stationary
Motion.correct_answer: turns about a fixed axis

Motion.text: Random motion, such as that of gas molecules, is characterized by
options: a perfectly predictable, repeating path
unpredictable, disordered movement with no fixed pattern
movement strictly along a straight line
movement only in a circular path
Motion.correct_answer: unpredictable, disordered movement with no fixed pattern

Motion.text: A contact force is one that
options: acts between bodies without them physically touching
requires direct physical contact between the interacting bodies
never actually exists in nature
only acts on stationary bodies
Motion.correct_answer: requires direct physical contact between the interacting bodies

Motion.text: A force field, such as gravitational or magnetic force, is one that
options: requires direct physical contact between bodies
can act between bodies without physical contact, through a region of influence
never has any measurable effect
only exists in a vacuum
Motion.correct_answer: can act between bodies without physical contact, through a region of influence

Motion.text: Speed is defined as
options: displacement per unit time, in a specified direction
distance travelled per unit time, without regard to direction
the rate of change of velocity
the same as acceleration
Motion.correct_answer: distance travelled per unit time, without regard to direction

Motion.text: Velocity is defined as
options: distance travelled per unit time, without direction
displacement per unit time, in a specified direction
the same as speed in every respect
the rate of change of displacement squared
Motion.correct_answer: displacement per unit time, in a specified direction

Motion.text: Acceleration is defined as the
options: distance travelled per unit time
rate of change of velocity with respect to time
same as velocity
total distance covered
Motion.correct_answer: rate of change of velocity with respect to time

Motion.text: The equation v = u + at is one of the equations of
options: uniformly accelerated motion, relating final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and time
simple harmonic motion only
circular motion only
projectile motion exclusively
Motion.correct_answer: uniformly accelerated motion, relating final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and time

Motion.text: The equation s = ut + ½at² relates
options: displacement, initial velocity, acceleration and time for uniformly accelerated motion
only speed and time
only mass and acceleration
only force and displacement
Motion.correct_answer: displacement, initial velocity, acceleration and time for uniformly accelerated motion

Motion.text: The equation v² = u² + 2as relates
options: final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and displacement, without involving time directly
only mass and velocity
only force and time
only displacement and time
Motion.correct_answer: final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and displacement, without involving time directly

Motion.text: For a body in free fall under gravity (ignoring air resistance), the acceleration is
options: zero
constant, approximately 9.8 m/s², directed downward
always increasing without limit
dependent on the mass of the falling body
Motion.correct_answer: constant, approximately 9.8 m/s², directed downward

Motion.text: On a distance-time graph, the gradient (slope) at any point represents the
options: acceleration at that point
speed at that point
displacement at that point
total distance travelled
Motion.correct_answer: speed at that point

Motion.text: On a velocity-time graph, the gradient (slope) at any point represents the
options: displacement at that point
acceleration at that point
speed at that point
total time elapsed
Motion.correct_answer: acceleration at that point

Motion.text: On a velocity-time graph, the area under the graph between two time values represents the
options: acceleration during that interval
displacement (or distance) covered during that interval
initial velocity only
final velocity only
Motion.correct_answer: displacement (or distance) covered during that interval

Motion.text: Instantaneous velocity refers to the
options: average velocity over an entire journey
velocity of a body at a specific, particular instant in time
velocity measured only at the start of motion
velocity that never changes
Motion.correct_answer: velocity of a body at a specific, particular instant in time

Motion.text: In projectile motion (ignoring air resistance), the horizontal component of velocity
options: constantly changes due to gravity
remains constant throughout the flight, since gravity acts only vertically
is always zero
increases continuously
Motion.correct_answer: remains constant throughout the flight, since gravity acts only vertically

Motion.text: In projectile motion, the vertical component of velocity
options: remains constant throughout the flight
changes continuously due to the constant downward acceleration of gravity
is always zero
is unaffected by gravity
Motion.correct_answer: changes continuously due to the constant downward acceleration of gravity

Motion.text: The maximum height reached by a projectile launched at an angle depends on
options: only the horizontal component of initial velocity
the vertical component of initial velocity and the acceleration due to gravity
only the total mass of the projectile
the colour of the projectile
Motion.correct_answer: the vertical component of initial velocity and the acceleration due to gravity

Motion.text: The time of flight of a projectile launched from and landing at the same height depends mainly on
options: the horizontal component of velocity only
the vertical component of initial velocity and gravitational acceleration
the total mass of the projectile
the horizontal distance travelled
Motion.correct_answer: the vertical component of initial velocity and gravitational acceleration

Motion.text: Newton’s first law of motion states that a body remains at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless
options: it experiences a net external force
it is observed by someone
it has zero mass
time stops
Motion.correct_answer: it experiences a net external force

Motion.text: Newton’s second law of motion relates force to
options: mass and velocity only
the rate of change of momentum of a body, or equivalently, mass times acceleration
displacement only
time only
Motion.correct_answer: the rate of change of momentum of a body, or equivalently, mass times acceleration

Motion.text: Newton’s third law of motion states that for every action, there is
options: no corresponding reaction
an equal and opposite reaction
a reaction of greater magnitude
a reaction of smaller magnitude
Motion.correct_answer: an equal and opposite reaction

Motion.text: Inertia refers to a body’s natural tendency to
options: accelerate spontaneously without any force
resist any change in its state of motion (rest or uniform velocity)
always come to rest
always increase in mass
Motion.correct_answer: resist any change in its state of motion (rest or uniform velocity)

Motion.text: Momentum is defined as the product of a body’s
options: mass and displacement
mass and velocity
force and time
mass and acceleration
Motion.correct_answer: mass and velocity

Motion.text: Impulse is defined as the product of
options: force and the time for which it acts
mass and velocity
mass and acceleration
displacement and time
Motion.correct_answer: force and the time for which it acts

Motion.text: The area under a force-time graph represents the
options: work done
impulse delivered
power developed
momentum before the force was applied
Motion.correct_answer: impulse delivered

Motion.text: The principle of conservation of linear momentum states that, in the absence of external forces, the total momentum of a system
options: always increases
remains constant before and after a collision or interaction
always decreases
becomes zero
Motion.correct_answer: remains constant before and after a collision or interaction

Motion.text: In circular motion, centripetal force is directed
options: tangent to the circular path
toward the centre of the circular path
away from the centre of the circular path
in a random direction
Motion.correct_answer: toward the centre of the circular path

Motion.text: Simple harmonic motion (S.H.M.) is characterized by
options: acceleration that is directly proportional to displacement from a fixed point and always directed toward that point
constant acceleration in one direction only
acceleration that has no relationship to displacement
motion that never repeats
Motion.correct_answer: acceleration that is directly proportional to displacement from a fixed point and always directed toward that point

Motion.text: In simple harmonic motion, the amplitude refers to the
options: time taken for one complete oscillation
maximum displacement from the equilibrium (mean) position
number of oscillations per second
velocity at the equilibrium position
Motion.correct_answer: maximum displacement from the equilibrium (mean) position

Gravitational Field.text: Newton’s law of universal gravitation states that the gravitational force between two masses is
options: directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them
inversely proportional to the product of their masses
independent of the distance between them
directly proportional to the distance between them, squared
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them

Gravitational Field.text: The universal gravitational constant, G, is
options: different for every pair of masses
a fundamental constant with the same value everywhere, used in Newton’s law of gravitation
equal to the acceleration due to gravity, g
not required in gravitational calculations
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: a fundamental constant with the same value everywhere, used in Newton’s law of gravitation

Gravitational Field.text: Gravitational potential at a point in a gravitational field is defined as
options: the force experienced by a unit mass placed at that point
the work done in bringing a unit mass from infinity to that point
the acceleration experienced at that point
unrelated to the concept of work
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: the work done in bringing a unit mass from infinity to that point

Gravitational Field.text: A conservative force field is one in which
options: the work done in moving a body between two points depends on the path taken
the work done in moving a body between two points is independent of the path taken
no work is ever done
forces vary randomly with time
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: the work done in moving a body between two points is independent of the path taken

Gravitational Field.text: The gravitational field is an example of a
options: non-conservative field
conservative field
field with no defined potential
field that does no work at all
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: conservative field

Gravitational Field.text: Frictional force is a typical example of a
options: conservative force
non-conservative force, since work done depends on the path taken
gravitational force
force with no relationship to path
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: non-conservative force, since work done depends on the path taken

Gravitational Field.text: The acceleration due to gravity, g, near the Earth’s surface has an approximate standard value of
options: 9.8 m/s²
1.0 m/s²
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: 9.8 m/s²

Gravitational Field.text: The value of g generally
options: is exactly the same everywhere on Earth’s surface, with no variation
varies slightly with latitude and altitude on the Earth’s surface
increases indefinitely as altitude increases
has no relationship to distance from Earth’s centre
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: varies slightly with latitude and altitude on the Earth’s surface

Gravitational Field.text: Mass differs from weight in that mass is
options: a vector quantity that varies with location, while weight is constant
a scalar quantity representing the amount of matter in a body, which remains constant regardless of location, while weight is a force that varies with gravitational field strength
identical to weight in every respect
measured only in newtons
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: a scalar quantity representing the amount of matter in a body, which remains constant regardless of location, while weight is a force that varies with gravitational field strength

Gravitational Field.text: The weight of a body is calculated as
options: mass divided by gravitational field strength
mass multiplied by gravitational field strength (W = mg)
mass multiplied by velocity
mass multiplied by distance
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: mass multiplied by gravitational field strength (W = mg)

Gravitational Field.text: Escape velocity refers to the minimum velocity needed for an object to
options: orbit the Earth indefinitely at a fixed altitude
completely escape a planet’s gravitational field without further propulsion
simply reach the top of a tall building
remain stationary relative to the Earth’s surface
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: completely escape a planet’s gravitational field without further propulsion

Gravitational Field.text: A parking orbit (geostationary orbit) is one in which a satellite
options: moves much faster than the Earth’s rotation
has an orbital period matching the Earth’s rotation period, appearing stationary relative to a point on Earth
falls back to Earth almost immediately
has no defined orbital period
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: has an orbital period matching the Earth’s rotation period, appearing stationary relative to a point on Earth

Gravitational Field.text: Weightlessness experienced by astronauts in orbit occurs because
options: gravity is completely absent in space
the astronaut and spacecraft are in continuous free-fall together, so there is no normal contact force to produce a sensation of weight
gravity suddenly disappears at high altitude
the spacecraft blocks all gravitational force
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: the astronaut and spacecraft are in continuous free-fall together, so there is no normal contact force to produce a sensation of weight

Gravitational Field.text: According to Newton’s law of gravitation, if the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes
options: twice as strong
one-quarter as strong
half as strong
four times as strong
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: one-quarter as strong

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why g decreases as altitude above the Earth’s surface increases?
options: The distance from the Earth’s centre increases, reducing the gravitational force per unit mass according to the inverse-square law
g always increases with altitude
g is completely independent of distance from Earth’s centre
Altitude has no relevance to gravitational field strength
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: The distance from the Earth’s centre increases, reducing the gravitational force per unit mass according to the inverse-square law

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why g varies slightly with latitude on the Earth’s surface?
options: The Earth is not a perfect sphere; it is slightly flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator, affecting the distance to the Earth’s centre
g is identical everywhere due to the Earth being a perfect sphere
Latitude has no bearing on gravitational field strength
g only varies with longitude, not latitude
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: The Earth is not a perfect sphere; it is slightly flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator, affecting the distance to the Earth’s centre

Gravitational Field.text: Gravitational potential energy of a body at a height h above a reference point is given by
options: mgh
½mv²
mg/h
m/gh
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: mgh

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why gravitational potential is usually taken to be zero at infinity, with negative values closer to a massive body?
options: Work must be done against the attractive gravitational force to move a mass away from a large body toward infinity, making potential increase (become less negative) with distance
Gravitational potential has no defined reference point
Gravitational potential is always positive everywhere
There is no relationship between gravitational potential and distance from a massive body
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Work must be done against the attractive gravitational force to move a mass away from a large body toward infinity, making potential increase (become less negative) with distance

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly relates escape velocity to the mass and radius of a planet?
options: Escape velocity increases with the planet’s mass and decreases with increasing radius, for a fixed mass
Escape velocity is completely independent of a planet’s mass and radius
Escape velocity decreases with increasing planetary mass
Escape velocity depends only on the planet’s radius, not its mass
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Escape velocity increases with the planet’s mass and decreases with increasing radius, for a fixed mass

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly describes the practical application of gravitational field concepts in satellite communication using geostationary orbits?
options: Satellites in geostationary orbit remain fixed relative to a point on Earth, allowing continuous communication coverage of a specific region
Geostationary satellites move independently of Earth’s gravitational field
Satellites in any orbit remain fixed relative to Earth’s surface
Gravitational field concepts have no application to satellite technology
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Satellites in geostationary orbit remain fixed relative to a point on Earth, allowing continuous communication coverage of a specific region

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a body’s weight would be different on the Moon compared to Earth, despite having the same mass in both locations?
options: The Moon has a different gravitational field strength than Earth, due to its different mass and radius, so the same mass experiences a different gravitational force (weight)
Mass changes when moved to the Moon, causing different weight
Weight is identical everywhere regardless of gravitational field strength
There is no relationship between weight and gravitational field strength
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: The Moon has a different gravitational field strength than Earth, due to its different mass and radius, so the same mass experiences a different gravitational force (weight)

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why work done against gravity in a conservative gravitational field depends only on the initial and final positions, not the path taken?
options: The gravitational force is conservative, so any energy expended moving away from a direct path is regained when returning toward the direct path, making net work path-independent
Gravitational work always depends heavily on the specific path taken
Gravity is a non-conservative force
Path independence only applies to non-conservative forces
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: The gravitational force is conservative, so any energy expended moving away from a direct path is regained when returning toward the direct path, making net work path-independent

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes why understanding gravitational fields is important for space exploration, such as calculating orbital trajectories and escape velocities?
options: Accurate application of gravitational principles allows precise calculation of the energy and velocity needed for launching, orbiting and escaping a planet’s gravitational field
Gravitational field concepts have no relevance to space exploration
Space exploration requires no consideration of gravitational forces
Escape velocity calculations are unrelated to gravitational field strength
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Accurate application of gravitational principles allows precise calculation of the energy and velocity needed for launching, orbiting and escaping a planet’s gravitational field

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why astronauts on the International Space Station, despite being within Earth’s gravitational field and experiencing significant gravitational force, appear “weightless”?
options: They are in continuous orbital free-fall around Earth, so there is no supporting contact force to create the sensation of weight, even though gravity is still acting on them
There is genuinely no gravitational force acting on the ISS or its occupants
The ISS is located entirely outside Earth’s gravitational field
Weightlessness in orbit has no connection to free-fall motion
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: They are in continuous orbital free-fall around Earth, so there is no supporting contact force to create the sensation of weight, even though gravity is still acting on them

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A system of coplanar forces is said to be in equilibrium when
options: the net force and net moment about any point are both zero
only the net force is zero, regardless of moments
the forces are all equal in magnitude
there is only one force acting
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the net force and net moment about any point are both zero

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The triangle law of forces states that if three coplanar forces acting at a point are in equilibrium, they can be represented by
options: the three sides of a triangle taken in order, in magnitude and direction
three unrelated, independent lines
only two sides of a triangle
a straight line only
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the three sides of a triangle taken in order, in magnitude and direction

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The polygon law of forces extends the triangle law to situations involving
options: only two forces
more than three coplanar forces in equilibrium, represented by the sides of a closed polygon
forces that are not coplanar
only forces along a single straight line
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: more than three coplanar forces in equilibrium, represented by the sides of a closed polygon

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Lami’s theorem applies to
options: any number of forces acting on a body
three coplanar, concurrent forces in equilibrium, relating each force to the sine of the angle between the other two
only two forces
forces that are not in equilibrium
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: three coplanar, concurrent forces in equilibrium, relating each force to the sine of the angle between the other two

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The moment of a force about a point is defined as
options: the force multiplied by the time it acts
the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the point to the line of action of the force
the force divided by distance
the same as the force itself
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the point to the line of action of the force

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A couple consists of
options: a single force acting on a body
two equal, parallel forces acting in opposite directions, with different lines of action, producing a turning effect (torque)
two forces acting in the same direction along the same line
only forces that act at a single point
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: two equal, parallel forces acting in opposite directions, with different lines of action, producing a turning effect (torque)

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The torque produced by a couple is calculated as
options: one of the forces multiplied by the perpendicular distance between the two forces
the sum of the two forces
the difference between the two forces
the product of the two forces divided by their distance apart
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: one of the forces multiplied by the perpendicular distance between the two forces

Equilibrium of Forces.text: For a rigid body to be in equilibrium under the action of several forces, it is necessary that
options: only the resultant force is zero
both the resultant force and the resultant moment (torque) about any point are zero
only the resultant moment is zero
all forces act at the same single point
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: both the resultant force and the resultant moment (torque) about any point are zero

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The resultant of a system of forces is
options: a single force that has the same overall effect as all the individual forces combined
always equal to zero
always equal to the largest individual force
unrelated to the individual forces
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: a single force that has the same overall effect as all the individual forces combined

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The equilibrant of a system of forces is
options: identical in magnitude and direction to the resultant
equal in magnitude to the resultant but acting in exactly the opposite direction
always zero
unrelated to the resultant
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: equal in magnitude to the resultant but acting in exactly the opposite direction

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The centre of gravity of a body is the point at which
options: the entire weight of the body may be considered to act
the body has zero mass
all forces on the body are equal
the body always experiences maximum acceleration
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the entire weight of the body may be considered to act

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A body is in stable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it
options: moves further away from its original position
tends to return to its original position
remains exactly where it was displaced to, with no tendency to move
immediately falls over
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: tends to return to its original position

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A body is in unstable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it
options: tends to return to its original position
tends to move further away from its original position
remains exactly at the displaced position
is unaffected by any displacement
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: tends to move further away from its original position

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A body is in neutral equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it
options: returns to its original position
moves further away from its original position
remains in its new position, with no tendency to move further or return
always falls immediately
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: remains in its new position, with no tendency to move further or return

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A body with a low centre of gravity and a wide base is generally
options: less stable than one with a high centre of gravity and narrow base
more stable than one with a high centre of gravity and narrow base
equally stable regardless of centre of gravity height or base width
always in unstable equilibrium
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: more stable than one with a high centre of gravity and narrow base

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The principle of moments states that for a body in rotational equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about a point equals the
options: sum of all forces acting on the body
sum of anticlockwise moments about the same point
mass of the body
sum of the linear momenta of the body
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: sum of anticlockwise moments about the same point

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A metre rule balanced on a pivot with weights at different distances illustrates
options: Newton’s third law only
the principle of moments
the law of conservation of energy only
Ohm’s law
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the principle of moments

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Resolving forces into two perpendicular directions is a useful technique for analysing equilibrium because it allows
options: each direction to be considered independently, simplifying the analysis of a multi- force system
forces to be ignored entirely
only vertical forces to ever be considered
equilibrium conditions to be established without considering direction
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: each direction to be considered independently, simplifying the analysis of a multi- force system

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly identifies a real-world application of the principle of moments?
options: A seesaw balancing when appropriately positioned weights are placed at different distances from the pivot
The principle of moments has no everyday applications
Moments apply only to purely theoretical, idealized systems
A seesaw’s balance is unrelated to the principle of moments
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: A seesaw balancing when appropriately positioned weights are placed at different distances from the pivot

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a ladder leaning against a wall can remain in equilibrium despite gravity acting on it?
options: The combined effects of the wall’s reaction force, the ground’s reaction force (and friction), and gravity satisfy both force and moment equilibrium conditions
A leaning ladder can never actually be in equilibrium
Only gravity needs to be considered for a leaning ladder’s equilibrium
Equilibrium of a leaning ladder requires no consideration of moments
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: The combined effects of the wall’s reaction force, the ground’s reaction force (and friction), and gravity satisfy both force and moment equilibrium conditions

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a tall, narrow object is more likely to topple over than a short, wide object of similar mass, when both are tilted by the same small angle?
options: The tall, narrow object’s centre of gravity moves outside its base of support more readily upon tilting, due to its higher centre of gravity and narrower base
Object shape and base width have no bearing on stability
A taller object always has a lower centre of gravity
Wider objects are always less stable than narrower ones
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: The tall, narrow object’s centre of gravity moves outside its base of support more readily upon tilting, due to its higher centre of gravity and narrower base

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains the design principle behind racing cars having a very low centre of gravity?
options: A low centre of gravity increases stability, reducing the likelihood of the car toppling over during high-speed cornering
A low centre of gravity has no effect on vehicle stability
Racing cars are designed with a high centre of gravity for improved stability
Centre of gravity height is irrelevant to cornering stability
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: A low centre of gravity increases stability, reducing the likelihood of the car toppling over during high-speed cornering

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly identifies why engineers apply the principle of moments when designing structures such as bridges and cranes?
options: Ensuring that clockwise and anticlockwise moments balance at supporting points is essential to prevent structural failure or toppling under load
The principle of moments has no relevance to structural engineering
Bridges and cranes require no consideration of turning effects or balance
Only the total weight of a structure matters, not how moments are distributed
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: Ensuring that clockwise and anticlockwise moments balance at supporting points is essential to prevent structural failure or toppling under load

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the general importance of understanding equilibrium of forces in mechanics?
options: It allows prediction and analysis of whether structures, objects and systems will remain stable under the combined effect of multiple forces
Equilibrium concepts are relevant only to purely theoretical, idealized problems
Real-world structures require no consideration of force or moment balance
Equilibrium of forces has no practical engineering application
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: It allows prediction and analysis of whether structures, objects and systems will remain stable under the combined effect of multiple forces

Work, Energy and Power.text: Work done by a force is defined as the product of
options: force and time
force and the displacement in the direction of the force
mass and velocity
force and mass
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: force and the displacement in the direction of the force

Work, Energy and Power.text: The SI unit of work and energy is the
options: newton
joule
watt
pascal
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: joule

Work, Energy and Power.text: Power is defined as the
options: total work done, regardless of time
rate at which work is done, or energy is transferred, per unit time
same as force
same as energy
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: rate at which work is done, or energy is transferred, per unit time

Work, Energy and Power.text: The SI unit of power is the
options: joule
newton
watt
pascal
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: watt

Work, Energy and Power.text: Kinetic energy of a moving body is given by the expression
options: mgh
½mv²
Fd
m/v
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: ½mv²

Work, Energy and Power.text: Gravitational potential energy of a body at height h is given by
options: ½mv²
mgh
Fd
m/gh
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: mgh

Work, Energy and Power.text: The principle of conservation of energy states that energy
options: can be created but not destroyed
can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed from one form to another
is always lost in any process
always increases over time
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed from one form to another

Work, Energy and Power.text: The area under a force-distance (force-displacement) graph represents the
options: power developed
work done
momentum
impulse
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: work done

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly lists two common energy transformations?
options: Chemical energy to electrical energy in a battery; electrical energy to heat energy in a resistor
Energy transformations do not actually occur in nature
Only mechanical energy can be transformed into other forms
Energy can only be transformed into heat, never any other form
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Chemical energy to electrical energy in a battery; electrical energy to heat energy in a resistor

Work, Energy and Power.text: Renewable energy sources are those that
options: become permanently depleted after a single use
are naturally replenished over relatively short timescales, such as solar, wind and hydroelectric energy
are limited exclusively to fossil fuels
cannot be used to generate electricity
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: are naturally replenished over relatively short timescales, such as solar, wind and hydroelectric energy

Work, Energy and Power.text: Non-renewable energy sources, such as coal and crude oil, are characterized by
options: being naturally replenished quickly
existing in finite quantities that are depleted much faster than they can naturally form
never being used for energy production
having no environmental impact
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: existing in finite quantities that are depleted much faster than they can naturally form

Work, Energy and Power.text: A significant environmental impact associated with burning fossil fuels for energy is
options: reduction of the greenhouse effect
increased greenhouse gas emissions, contributing to global warming
complete elimination of air pollution
no measurable environmental effect
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: increased greenhouse gas emissions, contributing to global warming

Work, Energy and Power.text: Energy diversification refers to the strategy of
options: relying on a single energy source exclusively
using a variety of different energy sources to improve reliability and sustainability of supply
eliminating all use of renewable energy
using only non-renewable energy sources
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: using a variety of different energy sources to improve reliability and sustainability of supply

Work, Energy and Power.text: Hydroelectric power generation, commonly associated with dams, works by
options: burning fossil fuels to generate steam
using the kinetic energy of falling or flowing water to turn turbines connected to generators
using solar panels exclusively
using nuclear fission exclusively
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: using the kinetic energy of falling or flowing water to turn turbines connected to generators

Work, Energy and Power.text: Dams for hydroelectric power are typically located
options: in flat, low-lying areas with no water flow
at sites with significant water flow and elevation difference, to maximize potential and kinetic energy conversion
only in desert regions
only where there is no river present
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: at sites with significant water flow and elevation difference, to maximize potential and kinetic energy conversion

Work, Energy and Power.text: Nuclear energy is primarily generated through the process of
options: combustion of nuclear fuel in air
nuclear fission, in which heavy atomic nuclei split, releasing large amounts of energy
simple chemical reactions
purely mechanical processes
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: nuclear fission, in which heavy atomic nuclei split, releasing large amounts of energy

Work, Energy and Power.text: Solar energy can be captured for practical use through
options: solar collectors and solar panels, which convert sunlight into heat or electrical energy
burning solar panels as fuel
processes entirely unrelated to sunlight
nuclear fission only
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: solar collectors and solar panels, which convert sunlight into heat or electrical energy

Work, Energy and Power.text: A solar panel typically converts
options: heat energy directly into chemical energy
light energy from the sun into electrical energy, via the photovoltaic effect
electrical energy into sunlight
mechanical energy into sunlight
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: light energy from the sun into electrical energy, via the photovoltaic effect

Work, Energy and Power.text: A solar collector, distinct from a solar panel, is primarily designed to
options: generate electricity directly
absorb and collect solar energy mainly as heat, for applications such as water heating
block sunlight completely
convert heat directly into sound energy
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: absorb and collect solar energy mainly as heat, for applications such as water heating

Work, Energy and Power.text: The global energy crisis generally refers to concerns about
options: an unlimited, permanently abundant supply of all energy sources
the balance between growing energy demand and the sustainability, cost, and environmental impact of energy supply
a complete absence of any energy sources worldwide
issues entirely unrelated to energy supply or demand
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: the balance between growing energy demand and the sustainability, cost, and environmental impact of energy supply

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains why energy conservation and efficient energy use are promoted as solutions to energy-related challenges?
options: Using energy more efficiently reduces overall demand, costs, and environmental impact, helping address supply challenges and sustainability concerns
Energy conservation has no meaningful effect on energy-related challenges
Efficient energy use always increases overall energy demand
Energy conservation is relevant only to non- renewable energy sources
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Using energy more efficiently reduces overall demand, costs, and environmental impact, helping address supply challenges and sustainability concerns

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains why calculating the work done using the area under a force-distance graph is useful when the force is not constant?
options: Integrating (finding the area under) a varying force-distance graph accounts for the changing force over the distance travelled, giving the correct total work done
The area under a force-distance graph has no relationship to work done when force varies
Work can only be calculated when force is constant
A varying force always does zero net work
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Integrating (finding the area under) a varying force-distance graph accounts for the changing force over the distance travelled, giving the correct total work done

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding energy sources and their environmental impact (as covered in “Energy and Society”) is relevant to national development?
options: Informed energy policy decisions, balancing supply, cost, and environmental impact, are important for sustainable economic growth and quality of life
Energy sources and their impacts have no relevance to national development
Environmental impact should never be considered in energy-related decisions
Energy policy is entirely disconnected from economic development
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Informed energy policy decisions, balancing supply, cost, and environmental impact, are important for sustainable economic growth and quality of life

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of the work-energy-power framework in physics?
options: It provides a unifying quantitative approach to analysing mechanical processes, energy transformations, and the rate at which work is performed across diverse physical systems
Work, energy, and power concepts have no unifying relevance across different physical systems
These concepts apply only to purely theoretical mechanics problems with no practical relevance
Energy transformations cannot be quantitatively analysed using this framework
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: It provides a unifying quantitative approach to analysing mechanical processes, energy transformations, and the rate at which work is performed across diverse physical systems

Friction.text: Static friction refers to the frictional force that
options: acts on a body already in motion
opposes the tendency of a stationary body to start moving
only acts on moving fluids
never actually exists between surfaces
Friction.correct_answer: opposes the tendency of a stationary body to start moving

Friction.text: Dynamic (kinetic) friction refers to the frictional force that
options: acts on a stationary body only
opposes the relative motion between two surfaces already sliding against each other
is always greater than static friction
never depends on the surfaces in contact
Friction.correct_answer: opposes the relative motion between two surfaces already sliding against each other

Friction.text: The coefficient of limiting friction is defined as the ratio of the
options: normal reaction to the limiting frictional force
limiting (maximum static) frictional force to the normal reaction between the surfaces
applied force to the weight of the body
mass to the area of contact
Friction.correct_answer: limiting (maximum static) frictional force to the normal reaction between the surfaces

Friction.text: A key advantage of friction in everyday life is that it
options: always wastes energy with no benefit
enables walking, and allows vehicle tyres to grip the road surface
always causes unwanted wear on machine parts
has no practical benefit whatsoever
Friction.correct_answer: enables walking, and allows vehicle tyres to grip the road surface

Friction.text: A key disadvantage of friction is that it
options: always helps conserve energy in machines
causes wear and tear on moving parts and results in energy loss as heat
has no negative effects at all
always improves the efficiency of machines
Friction.correct_answer: causes wear and tear on moving parts and results in energy loss as heat

Friction.text: Friction between machine parts can generally be reduced by
options: increasing the roughness of the surfaces in contact
using lubricants, such as oil or grease, between the surfaces
increasing the normal force between the surfaces
removing all surface contact entirely, which is always practical
Friction.correct_answer: using lubricants, such as oil or grease, between the surfaces

Friction.text: Viscosity refers to a fluid’s
options: colour
internal resistance to flow
density alone
temperature alone
Friction.correct_answer: internal resistance to flow

Friction.text: Terminal velocity of an object falling through a fluid is reached when
options: the object continues to accelerate indefinitely
the net force on the object becomes zero, as the upward resistive (drag) force balances the downward weight
the object suddenly stops completely
the object’s velocity becomes negative
Friction.correct_answer: the net force on the object becomes zero, as the upward resistive (drag) force balances the downward weight

Friction.text: Stoke’s law relates the viscous drag force on a small sphere moving through a fluid to
options: the sphere’s radius, the fluid’s viscosity, and the sphere’s velocity
only the sphere’s colour
only the fluid’s temperature
only the sphere’s mass
Friction.correct_answer: the sphere’s radius, the fluid’s viscosity, and the sphere’s velocity

Friction.text: According to Stoke’s law, the viscous drag force on a sphere is generally proportional to
options: the square of its radius only
its radius, its velocity, and the fluid’s viscosity
only its velocity, with no dependence on radius or viscosity
only its mass
Friction.correct_answer: its radius, its velocity, and the fluid’s viscosity

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between limiting static friction and dynamic friction for typical surfaces?
options: Limiting static friction is generally slightly greater than or equal to dynamic (kinetic) friction for the same pair of surfaces
Dynamic friction is always significantly greater than limiting static friction
They are always exactly equal in every situation
There is no meaningful relationship between the two
Friction.correct_answer: Limiting static friction is generally slightly greater than or equal to dynamic (kinetic) friction for the same pair of surfaces

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why it is generally harder to start pushing a heavy object than to keep it moving once it has started?
options: Static friction is typically greater than kinetic (dynamic) friction, requiring more force to overcome initially
Static friction is always less than kinetic friction
There is no difference between static and kinetic friction
Once moving, friction increases significantly compared to when stationary
Friction.correct_answer: Static friction is typically greater than kinetic (dynamic) friction, requiring more force to overcome initially

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why ball bearings are often used in rotating machine parts to reduce friction?
options: They convert sliding friction into rolling friction, which is generally significantly lower
Ball bearings increase the amount of friction present
Ball bearings have no effect on friction
Ball bearings work only by adding more surface contact area
Friction.correct_answer: They convert sliding friction into rolling friction, which is generally significantly lower

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a small, light object such as a feather reaches terminal velocity much sooner than a denser object of similar size, when both fall through air?
options: The feather’s relatively larger surface area to weight ratio means air resistance quickly balances its weight, resulting in earlier terminal velocity
Terminal velocity depends only on an object’s colour
Denser objects always reach terminal velocity before lighter objects of the same size
Air resistance has no relationship to an object’s surface area or weight
Friction.correct_answer: The feather’s relatively larger surface area to weight ratio means air resistance quickly balances its weight, resulting in earlier terminal velocity

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains a practical application of Stoke’s law, such as in determining the viscosity of a liquid using a falling sphere method?
options: By measuring the terminal velocity of a small sphere falling through the liquid, and applying Stoke’s law, the viscosity of the liquid can be calculated
Stoke’s law has no practical experimental application
Terminal velocity cannot be related to a fluid’s viscosity
Sphere size has no bearing on the calculation of viscosity via Stoke’s law
Friction.correct_answer: By measuring the terminal velocity of a small sphere falling through the liquid, and applying Stoke’s law, the viscosity of the liquid can be calculated

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why streamlining the shape of vehicles (such as cars and aircraft) helps improve fuel efficiency?
options: A streamlined shape reduces air resistance (a form of fluid friction/drag), reducing the energy needed to overcome this resistance during motion
Streamlining has no effect on air resistance
Streamlined shapes always increase air resistance
Fuel efficiency is entirely unrelated to a vehicle’s aerodynamic shape
Friction.correct_answer: A streamlined shape reduces air resistance (a form of fluid friction/drag), reducing the energy needed to overcome this resistance during motion

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why friction is essential for the proper functioning of vehicle brakes?
options: Friction between the brake pads and the wheel (or disc) converts the vehicle’s kinetic energy into heat, slowing the vehicle down
Friction plays no role in how vehicle brakes function
Brakes work by eliminating friction entirely between the relevant surfaces
Vehicle brakes function independently of any frictional forces
Friction.correct_answer: Friction between the brake pads and the wheel (or disc) converts the vehicle’s kinetic energy into heat, slowing the vehicle down

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why walking on an icy surface is generally more difficult than walking on a dry, rough surface?
options: Ice generally provides a much lower coefficient of friction than a dry, rough surface, reducing the grip needed for effective walking
Ice always provides more friction than a dry, rough surface
The coefficient of friction is identical for ice and rough dry surfaces
Friction has no relevance to the ease or difficulty of walking
Friction.correct_answer: Ice generally provides a much lower coefficient of friction than a dry, rough surface, reducing the grip needed for effective walking

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why increasing the surface roughness of two contacting surfaces generally increases the frictional force between them, up to a point?
options: Rougher surfaces generally have more microscopic interlocking irregularities that resist relative sliding motion
Surface roughness has no bearing on frictional force
Rougher surfaces always reduce frictional force between them
Frictional force depends only on the mass of the objects involved, not surface roughness
Friction.correct_answer: Rougher surfaces generally have more microscopic interlocking irregularities that resist relative sliding motion

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains the general relationship between the normal reaction force and limiting frictional force, as expressed by the coefficient of friction?
options: Limiting frictional force is generally directly proportional to the normal reaction force between the two surfaces, via the coefficient of friction
Frictional force is entirely independent of the normal reaction force
The coefficient of friction has no relationship to the normal reaction force
Limiting frictional force decreases as the normal reaction force increases
Friction.correct_answer: Limiting frictional force is generally directly proportional to the normal reaction force between the two surfaces, via the coefficient of friction

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains a practical disadvantage of high viscosity in engine lubricating oil under cold conditions?
options: Highly viscous oil flows more sluggishly in cold conditions, potentially reducing lubrication effectiveness and increasing engine start-up wear
High viscosity oil always flows more easily in cold conditions
Viscosity has no relationship to how an oil performs at different temperatures
Cold conditions have no effect on the viscosity of lubricating oils
Friction.correct_answer: Highly viscous oil flows more sluggishly in cold conditions, potentially reducing lubrication effectiveness and increasing engine start-up wear

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why raindrops falling through air eventually reach a roughly constant (terminal) velocity rather than accelerating indefinitely?
options: As speed increases, air resistance increases until it balances the raindrop’s weight, resulting in zero net force and constant velocity
Raindrops continue to accelerate indefinitely with no limiting factor
Air resistance has no effect on falling raindrops
Terminal velocity is unrelated to the balance between weight and air resistance
Friction.correct_answer: As speed increases, air resistance increases until it balances the raindrop’s weight, resulting in zero net force and constant velocity

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why oil is generally more effective than water as a lubricant for reducing friction between metal machine parts?
options: Oil generally has better adhesive and film-forming properties on metal surfaces, more effectively separating the surfaces and reducing direct contact
Water is always a more effective lubricant than oil for metal surfaces
Lubricant choice has no effect on the degree of friction reduction achieved
Oil and water are equally effective as lubricants in all situations
Friction.correct_answer: Oil generally has better adhesive and film-forming properties on metal surfaces, more effectively separating the surfaces and reducing direct contact

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of understanding friction, viscosity, and terminal velocity in engineering and everyday applications?
options: These concepts inform the design of efficient machines, vehicles, and structures, balancing the beneficial and detrimental effects of resistive forces
Friction and viscosity have no practical relevance to engineering or everyday life
Only theoretical physics, with no practical application, benefits from understanding these concepts
Terminal velocity has no relevance to real-world engineering problems
Friction.correct_answer: These concepts inform the design of efficient machines, vehicles, and structures, balancing the beneficial and detrimental effects of resistive forces

Simple Machines.text: A simple machine is a device that
options: always increases the total energy input into a system
enables a force applied at one point to overcome a load at another point, usually making work easier
can only be used to reduce the effort applied
never involves any mechanical advantage
Simple Machines.correct_answer: enables a force applied at one point to overcome a load at another point, usually making work easier

Simple Machines.text: The mechanical advantage of a machine is defined as the ratio of the
options: effort to the load
load to the effort applied
velocity ratio to efficiency
work output to work input, expressed as a ratio only when they are equal
Simple Machines.correct_answer: load to the effort applied

Simple Machines.text: The velocity ratio of a machine is defined as the ratio of the
options: distance moved by the load to the distance moved by the effort
distance moved by the effort to the distance moved by the load, in the same time
load to the effort
work output to work input
Simple Machines.correct_answer: distance moved by the effort to the distance moved by the load, in the same time

Simple Machines.text: The efficiency of a machine is defined as the ratio of
options: mechanical advantage to velocity ratio, usually expressed as a percentage
load to effort only
effort to load only
input force to output force, without regard to distance moved
Simple Machines.correct_answer: mechanical advantage to velocity ratio, usually expressed as a percentage

Simple Machines.text: For an ideal (perfectly efficient) machine, the mechanical advantage would be
options: always greater than the velocity ratio
equal to the velocity ratio, giving 100% efficiency
always zero
unrelated to the velocity ratio
Simple Machines.correct_answer: equal to the velocity ratio, giving 100% efficiency

Simple Machines.text: In practice, the efficiency of real machines is generally
options: always exactly 100%, with no energy losses
less than 100%, due to energy losses such as friction
always greater than 100%
completely unrelated to friction
Simple Machines.correct_answer: less than 100%, due to energy losses such as friction

Simple Machines.text: A lever is a simple machine that operates on the principle of
options: fluid pressure
moments (turning effect of forces) about a pivot (fulcrum)
electromagnetic induction
refraction of light
Simple Machines.correct_answer: moments (turning effect of forces) about a pivot (fulcrum)

Simple Machines.text: In a first-class lever, the fulcrum is positioned
options: between the effort and the load
at the same end as the effort
at the same end as the load
it does not have a defined fulcrum position
Simple Machines.correct_answer: between the effort and the load

Simple Machines.text: In a wheel and axle system, mechanical advantage is gained mainly because
options: the wheel and axle have identical radii
the effort is applied at the larger radius (wheel) while the load acts at the smaller radius (axle), or vice versa depending on configuration
there is no relationship between the radii and mechanical advantage
the wheel and axle system cannot provide any mechanical advantage
Simple Machines.correct_answer: the effort is applied at the larger radius (wheel) while the load acts at the smaller radius (axle), or vice versa depending on configuration

Simple Machines.text: A pulley system is a simple machine used mainly to
options: change the direction and/or magnitude of an applied force to lift loads more easily
generate electrical energy directly
measure temperature
measure time intervals
Simple Machines.correct_answer: change the direction and/or magnitude of an applied force to lift loads more easily

Simple Machines.text: An inclined plane provides mechanical advantage by allowing a load to be raised using
options: a smaller effort over a longer distance, compared to lifting it vertically
a larger effort over a shorter distance
no effort at all
effort and distance identical to direct vertical lifting
Simple Machines.correct_answer: a smaller effort over a longer distance, compared to lifting it vertically

Simple Machines.text: A screw can be considered a simple machine based on the principle of
options: the lever
an inclined plane wound around a cylinder
fluid pressure
electromagnetic induction
Simple Machines.correct_answer: an inclined plane wound around a cylinder

Simple Machines.text: If a machine has a mechanical advantage of 4 and a velocity ratio of 5, its efficiency is
Which of the following correctly explains why the efficiency of a real machine is always less than 100%?
options: Some input energy is always lost to friction and other resistive forces, rather than being entirely converted into useful output work
Real machines always convert 100% of input energy into useful work
Efficiency losses only occur in electrical machines, not mechanical ones
There is no relationship between friction and machine efficiency
